Is a supply chain really a chain?

A straight line from supplier to customer is useful for explaining the basic sequence—but it hides most of the real supply network.

1
One visible route

The familiar chain shows one possible path from raw materials to the customer.

2
Many hidden connections

Other suppliers, sites, warehouses, and partners sit behind that path.

3
Decisions everywhere

Each node makes choices that can affect many other parts of the network.

Your task:

reveal the realistic elements that may be hidden behind a simplified supply chain.

Key takeaway

Think network, not line.

We still call it a supply chain, but the chain is usually only one route through a much larger and interconnected network.

A supply chain is an interconnected network

It may include hundreds or thousands of suppliers, sites, warehouses, manufacturers, logistics providers, retailers, and customer channels.

  1. 1
    Many nodes

    Several suppliers, facilities, partners, and customer channels may be involved.

  2. 2
    Many routes

    The same product can move through different paths depending on the situation.

  3. 3
    Interdependent decisions

    A choice or disruption at one node can affect many other parts of the network.

Remember: The straight chain remains useful—but it is a simplified view of the real supply network.
